The Twitch article describes a subscription revenue split policy where Twitch shares subscription revenue with creators. Through the Partner Plus program launched in June, eligible creators receive a 70/30 subscription revenue split on the first $100,000 they make per year. Eligibility is based on a points-based system, where Tier 1, 2, and 3 subs earn 1, 2, and 6 points respectively, with a threshold of 350 monthly paid subscriptions (gift subs and Amazon Prime monthly subs don't count toward the original criteria). Twitch's broader strategy involves three monetization pillars: community-based support (subscriptions, gifting, cheering), advertising (with increased rev share and an ad incentive program), and sponsorships (where they are behind and now focusing on growth through Amazon advertising).

The Beeper Mini article describes a direct consumer subscription model where the app was originally priced at $1.99 per month for users to access iMessage chats on Android. However, due to the "chaotic" situation following Apple's attempt to shut down the service, Beeper decided to make Beeper Mini free for the time being, stating "As soon as things stabilize (we hope they will), we'll look at turning on subscriptions again."

The strategies differ in that Twitch's model involves revenue sharing with content creators across multiple streams (subs, ads, sponsorships) on a platform, while Beeper Mini uses a straightforward direct-to-consumer monthly subscription fee for app access, which has been temporarily suspended to make the app free.
